newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Barbados puts up native son for U.N. health job.
newsitem.headline: Barbados puts up native son for U.N. health job.

text.p: Barbados on Wednesday proposed the chief of the Pan American Health Organisation, Sir George Alleyne, as a candidate to take over the leadership of the World Health Organisation (WHO) next year.
Sir George, a former Dean of the Faculty of Medicine of the University of the West Indies, joins three other candidates for the post.
The current WHO director-general, Hiroshi Nakajima of Japan, announced last week that he would step down in July 1998 at the end of his second five-year mandate.

Proposing Sir George during a session of the two-week WHO Assembly in Geneva, Barbados' Health and Environment Minister H.Elizabeth Thompson described him as "an outstanding leader" as well as a distinguished public health practitioner.

The three other candidates announced so far are Nafis Sadik of Pakistan, head of the United Nations Population Fund, Gro Harlem Brundtland, former prime minister of Norway, and Fernando Antezana Aranibar of Bolivia, a Nakajima deputy.
The WHO's Executive Committee will make its own recommendation next January and the final decision will be taken at the next WHO Assembly in May 1998.
